c.tagline: Medieval towers, porticoes, and legendary cuisine.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU number with interpreter support; 113 reaches the state police directly and 118 the ambulance service.

hood_landmark.Quadrilatero: medieval market lanes packed with food stalls and historic delis
hood_landmark.Santo Stefano: Basilica di Santo Stefano, the 'Seven Churches' complex
hood_landmark.Bolognina: the Mercato Albani covered market and the quarter's street art
hood_landmark.Saragozza: Portico di San Luca, the 666-arch climb to the Sanctuary of San Luca
hood_landmark.San Donato: the BolognaFiere exhibition district and Grand Tour Italia (former FICO) food park

avoid.reason: Pickpockets target the train station, Via dell'Indipendenza and crowded porticoes, and the Piazza Verdi university zone gets rowdy with drug dealing late at night.

hood_desc: Quadrilatero is the medieval market grid right behind Piazza Maggiore, packed with delis, wine bars and food stalls; ideal for first-time visitors and food lovers who want to be in the buzzing historic heart, though it gets crowded and touristy.

Santo Stefano centers on the beautiful basilica complex and its piazza, an elegant, atmospheric quarter of porticoed streets and aperitivo spots; suits those wanting classic Bologna charm and a refined but lively evening scene.

Bolognina is a gritty, multicultural former working-class district north of the station, now gentrifying with cheaper rents, ethnic eateries and a creative edge; good for budget travelers and those who prefer real local life over polish.

Saragozza is a quieter, residential and well-off zone leading up to the famous portico walk to San Luca; suits families and travelers who want calm, greenery and an authentic neighborhood feel within reach of the center.

San Donato is a large residential and university district east of the center with student energy, parkland and affordable housing; best for longer stays, students and visitors happy to trade central location for value and everyday local vibe.

water.note: Tap water meets EU standards and is safe to drink, though locals often prefer bottled for taste.

transit.pay: A single Tper ticket costs EUR 2.30 (about USD 2.70), valid 75 minutes; buy it at tabaccherie, newsstands and machines, or pay EUR 2.50 in coins at the onboard machine. Easiest option: tap a contactless bank card or phone on the validator when boarding (EUR 2.30, best fare applied automatically), or use the Roger app; a day ticket is EUR 9. The Marconi Express monorail to the airport is separate, EUR 12.80 one way (about USD 15), payable online, at station machines or by contactless tap at the gates.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:30am to midnight; a network of dedicated night lines covers late-night hours, especially on weekends.

transit.m: Marconi Express monorail to Bologna Centrale, 7 min
